title: Fish Tacos
subtitle: Battered cod in soft tacos with avocado and lime
excerpt: Light battered cod strips served in warm tacos with avocado, soured cream, and fresh coriander. A squeeze of lime over everything brings it together.
sourceNotes: Inspired by Baja California-style fish tacos. Beer batter is the most common approach; this version uses a simple milk batter.

recipe.temperatureNote: Oil for frying should reach 180 degrees C

content.text: Get all the toppings ready before you start frying. The battered fish is best eaten straight from the oil.

items.prepNote: for the batter, plus extra for dusting

content.text: Prepare all toppings first. Slice the avocado, pick the coriander, and cut the lime into wedges.
Whisk the flour, milk, cumin, and chilli flakes together to make a smooth batter. Season well.
Pour the oil into the stockpot. Heat over medium-high heat to 180 degrees C.
Dust the fish strips lightly in plain flour, then dip into the batter. Let the excess drip off.
Fry in batches of 4 to 5 strips for 3 to 4 minutes until golden. Do not crowd the pan.
Lift out with a slotted spoon. Drain on kitchen paper. Keep warm in a low oven while you fry the rest.
Serve the fish in warm tortillas or lettuce leaves with avocado, soured cream, coriander, and lime.

items.symptom: Batter is thick and doughy rather than light.
items.cause: Batter was too thick or oil was not hot enough.
items.fix: Thin batter with a splash of milk; check oil is at 180 degrees C.

items.symptom: Fish falls apart in the oil.
items.cause: Strips were too thin or the dust layer was skipped.
items.fix: Dust with flour before battering to help it stick.

items.symptom: Oil temperature dropped after adding fish.
items.cause: Too many pieces added at once.
items.fix: Fry in smaller batches and let oil recover between each.
